## [Projects](/research/projects/)
### Deep-Sea Sediment Monitoring

Sediment plumes are at the heart of the environmental impacts of deep-sea mining. Predicting how far a plume spreads requires the size and settling velocity of the suspended particles, which aggregate and break apart in ways that cannot be reproduced by bringing samples to the surface. A prototype of the [RTSSV particle camera](/research/projects/RTSSV) was previously deployed on collector vehicle trials to observe particle size and shape, and its first field deployment on a gimbaled bottom lander took place in [Halifax Harbour](/research/projects/OAE_Halifax) in October 2025.

We are building out a bottom lander rated to 6000 m for benthic sediment transport science and deep-sea mining monitoring. It carries the gimbaled RTSSV, a five-beam ADCP with echosounder, a CTD with turbidity sensor, dual acoustic releases, and a lithium battery for month-long deployments.
